clue.text: Humiliated band half-heartedly backing O'Connor

indicators.note: the heart of the band's name is its doubled middle letter, and only half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: ABBA is the Swedish pop group

indicators.note: backing means the name comes in reversed, read from its end to its start

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

explanation.surface: A band, playing without full conviction behind a veteran crooner, is left feeling humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' takes one B from the middle of ABBA, leaving ABA; 'backing' turns DES into SED. Des O'Connor was a long-running British television host and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abased has been lowered in dignity, a direct synonym for humiliated.

clue.text: Let slip that solicitor follows a band

indicators.note: follows places the solicitor's word after the band's name

parts.note: Blur is the British Britpop group
a tout solicits custom, so one who touts is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: A lawyer is said to have let something slip while trailing after a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' wants to mean a British lawyer; here it is one who solicits trade, a TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To blurt something out is to let it slip, saying it suddenly and indiscreetly.

clue.text: Planes move slowly by plant

parts.note: to plane wood is to smooth it, as one sands it
to edge forward is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: Aircraft taxi slowly past some vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' reads as aircraft but is the carpenter's verb, SANDS. 'by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand sedge is a grass-like coastal species of sedge, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Ambitious band finally split

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word band

parts.note: riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A driven group of musicians eventually breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: A driven person is highly motivated and ambitious.

clue.text: Plant flower, heading off to record store

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: a disk records and stores data

explanation.surface: A horticultural note: plant your flowers, then head to the record shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's river, here the TAMAR on the Devon-Cornwall border in England; 'heading off' strips D from DISK.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery shrub or small tree, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Everything depends on band member harbouring female outlaw

parts.note: The Who are the English rock band

indicators.note: harbouring means the limb's letters hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
she is the female pronoun
to outlaw is to ban

explanation.surface: Everything hinges on a musician sheltering a female fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' sets SHEBAN inside LEG, giving LESHEBANG after THE WHO. 'depends on' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang is an idiom for the entire lot, everything involved.

clue.text: Most inadequate jockey agrees to board mount

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so these letters go inside the mount's abbreviation

parts.note: Mt is the abbreviation for mount, a mountain

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters of agrees are moved about

explanation.surface: A rider consents to climb on to the horse that is least fit for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' and 'mount' paint a racecourse, but 'jockey' is the anagram signal and 'to board' sets the jumbled letters inside the mount's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient, so the superlative is the most inadequate.

clue.text: River animal mounting small steps

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: in a down entry mounting means going up, so the beast's letters read bottom to top

parts.note: the gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A creature climbs up from the riverbank by a few little steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The rungs of a ladder are its steps.

clue.text: Band of 6 topless models

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

parts.note: the figure 6 is spelt as the word six

explanation.surface: A group of six models appearing without their tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun for the women in the picture but is the anagram verb: SIX with TOPLESS reshaped gives SEXPISTOLS. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sex Pistols were the 1970s English punk group, so they are a band.

clue.text: Poet gets fish by a whisker

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: A poet lands a fish and wins by the narrowest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a whisker' reads as 'only just'; 'by a' is a link and 'whisker' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnside is a style of facial hair, the original of the sideburn, so a whisker.

clue.text: Queen has note about wrong extension

indicators.note: about means the queen and the note go around the next piece

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714
E is a note of the musical scale
a cross, X, marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: Her Majesty has a memo about a mistaken building extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts X between ANNE and E, so the queen and note sit either side of the cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an extension.

clue.text: Quiet record gathers support shortly after meal

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an EP is an extended-play record
to herd animals is to gather them

indicators.note: shortly means the word for support loses its last letter

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: A soft song on vinyl brings the crowd together shortly after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SH, EP and HERDS run in order, then PIER cut short to PIE. Shepherd's pie is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is a dish eaten as a main course, so it is a meal.

clue.text: Band given minutes to produce music thus

parts.note: a tape is a narrow strip or band of material
the minutes of a meeting are its record

explanation.surface: A group handed the meeting notes makes music this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' points back to the wordplay: tape plus record is how the music is produced. 'given' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape-record is to capture sound on magnetic tape, one way of making recorded music.

clue.text: Singer banned from listening

indicators.note: from listening tells us the word for banned is heard, not read

parts.note: barred means prohibited or banned

explanation.surface: A vocalist is excluded from a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from listening' looks like the singer was barred from a hearing; it is the cue to say BARRED out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet in the old sense of one who sang epic verses.

clue.text: Purify the Italian rejected from front of show

indicators.note: rejected from front of means these letters are thrown off the start of the next word

parts.note: to illustrate a point is to show it
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian is sent away from the head of a show to cleanse it.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed version was LAST-GASP with a different clue; this is the corrected clue, and the grid entry here is LUSTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to purify by ritual washing or sacrifice, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Corrupt president sent up theatre equipment

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to corrupt is to rot
Jimmy Carter was the 39th US president

explanation.surface: A crooked head of state is lampooned on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' sounds like satire but turns ROTCARTER around. 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a surgical instrument holding a wound open, kit used in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Equipment given to one into cooking Italian food

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
a means one

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being concocted into something new

explanation.surface: Kitchen kit is handed to someone keen on preparing Italian dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges A and INTO to ATONI. 'given to' is a link joining RIG to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ridged tube pasta, an Italian food.

clue.text: Helps mount suspect images

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
E-fits are computer-built likenesses of suspects issued by the police

explanation.surface: Someone helps put up pictures of wanted criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a verb for hanging the images; it is BEN. An E-FIT is the British police's composite picture of a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefits are advantages or welfare payments, things that help, as the verb does here in noun form.

clue.text: Crystal clear piece of mineral

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A transparent fragment of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft magnesium silicate, a mineral used for talcum powder.

clue.text: Shop where a band may be seen

definitions.meaning: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police

definitions.text: where a band may be seen
definitions.meaning: a ring or wedding band is worn on this digit

explanation.surface: A store where a musical group might be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' wants to be a store; it is the British slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is to identify them to the police, and a ring band is worn on a finger.

clue.text: A holy day one month before writer returns with, say, gold

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

indicators.note: returns means the writer's name and what follows it come back in reverse

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, the English novelists
eg, for example, is what say means here
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A festival falls a month before an author comes back with treasure, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reads backwards the writer, the 'say' word and the gold symbol together, giving UAGESIMA; 'before' and 'with' are links. Septuagesima is the old church name for the Sunday about seventy days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuagesima is the third Sunday before Lent in the church calendar, a holy day.

clue.text: A metaphor, perhaps: "A band not suitable for all"

indicators.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages, so not having it drops that letter

parts.note: a troupe is a band of performers

explanation.surface: A warning that a group's act is not family-friendly, by way of figurative speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not suitable for all' looks like a content warning; it removes U, the film rating for universal viewing in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, of which a metaphor is one example.

clue.text: See 2
Band member brought over a close relative of his

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of U2
b/o is the bookkeeping abbreviation for brought over

explanation.surface: A rock star brings across one of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' looks like a verb about the singer; it is B/O, the accountant's note for a balance carried forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonobo is an ape regarded as one of humankind's nearest living relatives.

clue.text: Physicist has dreadful feeling in front of record store

indicators.note: in front of places the feeling before the store

parts.note: angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety
ROM, read-only memory, is a store of recorded data

explanation.surface: A scientist feels dread outside a music shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record store' reads as a music shop; it is computer memory, ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Angstrom was a Swedish physicist, after whom a unit of length is named.

clue.text: Becoming attached to band after getting head turned

indicators.note: after getting says the band's word follows the reworked head
turned means the letters of head are twisted into a new order

parts.note: a ring is a band, as in a wedding band

explanation.surface: Joining a group once one's head has been turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head turned' suggests flattery; here 'turned' is the anagram signal, giving ADHE, and 'after getting' puts the band word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhering means sticking to, so becoming attached.

clue.text: Right to include one in cultural curio

indicators.note: to include means the cultural word takes in the next letter

parts.note: arty means interested in the arts, cultural
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An object of genuine cultural interest is correct to put in the collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something rare and prized, which is what a curio is.
